Commercial property condition assessments in Columbia, SC: what to expect (2026)

Published 2026-11-16

If you are buying, refinancing or holding commercial property in Columbia, South Carolina, a property condition assessment (PCA) tells you what condition the building is really in and what it is likely to cost over the next several years. This guide explains what a PCA covers, what to ask about in the Midlands, and how to order one.

What a commercial PCA covers in Columbia

A PCA is a documented walk-through and records review of a commercial property, usually written to the ASTM E2018 standard. For retail strip centers, office buildings, multifamily, and industrial and flex space, the report typically covers:

  • Roof and roof drainage
  • Structure, foundation and building envelope
  • HVAC, electrical and plumbing systems
  • Life-safety and accessibility observations
  • Site, paving, drainage and parking areas
  • Immediate repairs and a schedule of expected capital needs

The exact scope depends on your assignment. Agree the standard, exclusions and deliverables in writing before fieldwork starts.

What to ask about in the Midlands

Columbia's hot, humid summers put heavy demand on HVAC equipment, so cooling systems and roofs deserve close attention. Ask for the age, condition and remaining useful life of each rooftop unit, not just a general comment.

Many Midlands retail and office properties have large flat roofs and extensive paved parking. Request notes on roof membrane condition, ponding, seams and flashing, and on pavement cracking and drainage.

If you are buying an investment property from a seller who has deferred maintenance, ask the assessor to separate immediate repairs from replacements that can be budgeted over the reserve period.

How to order a PCA in Columbia

  1. Define the decision. Say whether the report supports an acquisition, a refinance, a lender requirement or an internal capital plan.
  2. Collect lender requirements. Get the lender's written report requirements before you request a proposal.
  3. Send property details. Provide the address, property type, size, year built, known issues and your deadline.
  4. Arrange access. Ask the seller or property manager to confirm roof, equipment room and tenant space access before the site visit.
  5. Review the draft. Trace each major finding back to its photos and observations, then assign an owner to every open item.

What a PCA does not replace

A PCA reports on physical conditions that can be observed. It does not replace an environmental site assessment, a zoning report, a title review, lease review or legal advice. Concealed defects and untested systems may need specialist follow-up, and local code, permitting and flood-zone questions should be confirmed with the relevant authorities.

Frequently asked questions

Who performs commercial property condition assessments in Columbia, SC?

C&J Property Assessments performs commercial property condition assessments for investors, lenders and funds in South Carolina, including Columbia, Lexington and the Midlands. Confirm the assessor, standard, scope and deliverables in a written proposal before you engage anyone.

What does a commercial PCA cover?

A PCA documents the observed physical condition of a property's major systems, such as roof, structure, building envelope, HVAC, electrical, plumbing, site and paving, and identifies repairs and expected capital needs. It is not a substitute for environmental, legal, title or lease review.

Does a PCA follow ASTM E2018?

Commercial PCAs are commonly performed to the ASTM E2018 standard. Ask the proposal to name the edition and state any exclusions or departures, and confirm what your lender requires.

How quickly can I get a report?

Does a PCA include environmental or zoning review?

No. Environmental site assessments and zoning reports are separate products. Confirm with your lender and advisers whether you need them alongside the PCA.
